Everything below, including the rotation, the TEU and the vsProforma figures, is the 21 Sep 2026 scrape carried forward verbatim; lastSeen is deliberately left at 2026-09-21 so the staleness is visible. missedRuns was NOT incremented because Maersk was never queried - absence of a sighting here is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. The Yantian departure of 23 Sep 2026 falls in ISO week 39 and so is still inside this run window. --- CARRIED-FORWARD DETECTOR CAUTION: DETECTOR CAUTION on this source. The Maersk routing API exposes a boolean isRoutingAdhoc. On CNYTN-USHOU it is true only for this XL row and false for all eight TP15 rows, which looks like a clean ad-hoc label. On KRPUS-USHOU it is true for EVERY row including all eight TP15 proforma sailings. It therefore behaves like a per-pair routing attribute, not an ad-hoc marker, and must be treated as context only - the same way isGemini is - never as a trigger. This voyage stays classified as an extra loader on the strength of the serviceName XL / serviceCode 770 being absent from every alliance registry, not on that flag. vsProforma uses the modal TP15 transit observed this run (33 days across 4 of 8 sailings); the 17 Sep record used 34, so the 1-day move in deltaDays is a proforma-side change, not a slip.

Consequence beyond ONE itself: Yang Ming and HMM tonnage normally reaches this tracker only through ONE under EC1-EC4, so both carriers have zero coverage this run.

Lanes NOT covered this run. (1) ISO weeks 44-46 have no Evergreen coverage at all: durationWeek caps at 28 days, so the first pass reached only 20 Oct 2026, and the second pass at departureDay 20 Oct was refused with ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED after roughly ten requests. Hapag-Lloyd did cover the full window. (2) CMA CGM: zero lanes, skipped on purpose to protect the shared DataDome quota. (3) MSC, ZIM, ONE, Maersk: zero lanes, see the SOURCE BLOCKED entries. (4) Evergreen Ningbo-Houston and Ningbo-Savannah were lost to the throttle mid-sweep. (5) Budget origins Xiamen, Qingdao, Singapore, Port Klang and Kaohsiung were queried on Hapag only (Xiamen and Qingdao returned no direct single-leg service) and not on Evergreen.

AUG surfaced on Evergreen CNYTN-USHOU with n 2 in a 28-day window, which by the n<=2 rule is an XL candidate. The TVS2 VesselSchedule drill-down on EVER LUCKY (vslCode LUKY) settled it: LINE: Asia-U.S. GULF Service(AUG), rotation Kaohsiung - Cai Mep - Yantian - Ningbo - Pusan - Panama Canal - Houston - Mobile, with a matching 085W westbound leg. A fixed round-trip rotation with a named trade lane is a proforma Gulf service, not an ad-hoc voyage; two sailings in four weeks is simply a fortnightly cadence. AUG added to serviceRegistry under Ocean Alliance so it stops triggering.

NSB (n 5) and KTH (n 4) appeared on Evergreen KRPUS-USNYC and would otherwise trip the unknown-code-with-n>=3 rule. Every one of their voyage numbers ends in S, not E, and their transits run 43-53 days against 22-32 days for the direct NUE/NUE2 sailings on the same pair: these are southbound feeder first legs of transhipment routings, not direct services. Both codes were already on ignoredCodes from an earlier run and stay there. No promotion.

No OGEC voyage 0022 anywhere this run. Voyages 0020 (TRITON, sailed 2 Sep, now in history) and 0021 (EVER LASTING) were consecutive and roughly a week apart, which is why OGEC was called a rolling programme. Evergreen only reached 20 Oct this run, so a late-October or November 0022 would sit in the blind spot rather than being genuinely absent. Do not conclude the programme has stopped on this run alone.
